simple.meaning: יְצֻקָה (yᵉtsuqâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “poured out , i.e. run into a mould.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 1 Kings, beginning at 1 Kings 7:24. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְצֻקָה (H3333) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יְצֻקָה (yᵉtsuqâh) / H3333 is traced through 1 Kings 7:24, 1 Kings 7:30 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Under its brim around there were buds which encircled it for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The buds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.

timeline.evidenceText: Under its brim around there were buds which encircled it for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The buds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
Every base had four bronze wheels, and axles of bronze; and the four feet of it had supports. The supports were cast beneath the basin, with wreaths at the side of each.
